spec_features.spec_quote: Small `max_steps` (default 12) — enough to see onset, capped to bound cost.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:79 `for i in range(max_steps):` bounds the episode loop; default `max_steps: int = 12` at agent.py:57 and runner.py:37. When the loop exhausts, `stop_reason='max_steps'` (agent.py:75) is returned. The cap is read and enforced end-to-end (runner passes cfg.max_steps -> run_episode).
spec_features.notes: This is a genuine enforced loop bound that ends the episode. It is the only mechanism that bounds the subject's exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Repeat until one of: `max_steps` reached, `give_up`/`escalate` called, or the model emits no tool call
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: the `for i in range(max_steps)` loop terminates on (a) loop exhaustion; (b) terminal tool: dispatch returns is_terminal True for give_up/escalate (tools.py:90-94), agent.py sets `terminal=True` and `if terminal: break` (agent.py ~115-117); (c) stall: `if not tool_calls: stop_reason='stalled'; break` (agent.py ~120-122). All three branches actually execute and stop the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three documented stop conditions are wired and enforced.

spec_features.evidence: Both tools are in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py:50-78) and listed in the SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:21-33). dispatch() handles both returning is_terminal=True (tools.py:90-94). agent.py reads is_terminal, sets stop_reason='gave_up'/'escalated', and breaks the loop. So the subject can actually invoke either tool to immediately end the episode.
spec_features.notes: Tool is both delivered to the subject AND honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We expose BOTH `give_up` and `escalate` as first-class tools so the model can cleanly signal either terminal state, and we can measure them directly rather than only inferring from prose.
